sentences.text: A case report describes a 22-year-old male with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, confirmed by specific antibodies in his cerebrospinal fluid, who developed neuropsychiatric symptoms and generalized seizures.

Initial continuous EEG monitoring showed diffuse slowing that did not align with his movement disorders, but after the seizure burden decreased, a definite extreme delta brush pattern emerged synchronized with right-sided jaw and arm movements.

In this patient, the extreme delta brush pattern was identified as an ictal phenomenon rather than a non-epileptic one, suggesting it may represent ictal activity in some instances contrary to the classic view of it as a non-ictal biomarker.
The authors conclude that continuous EEG monitoring is necessary to differentiate between seizures and dyskinesias and to understand the potential ictal nature of these patterns.
